intended_object: The canonical inclusion homomorphism N → N ⋊ G of the normal factor into the internal semidirect product of group objects in a cartesian monoidal category. Internally it is the map n ↦ (n, 1), i.e. `lift (𝟙 N) 1`. The docstring and the module documentation say this.
explanation:
The library builds the semidirect product `A.semidirectProduct` on the object `N ⊗ G`. Its group-object structure is chosen so that, for every object X, the group of maps X ⟶ N ⊗ G is the ordinary `SemidirectProduct` of the groups of maps X ⟶ N and X ⟶ G. These groups vary naturally in X; they are the "generalized points" of the objects.

`inl` is defined as follows. `inlNatTrans` applies the ordinary `SemidirectProduct.inl` (n ↦ ⟨n, 1⟩) at each X, which gives a natural transformation of group-valued functors. This is composed with the isomorphism `pointIso.inv`. Then the fully faithful Yoneda embedding `yonedaGrp` turns the result back into a morphism of internal groups. The proved lemma `pointMulEquiv_comp_inl` confirms that on generalized points the map is `SemidirectProduct.inl`. So the underlying morphism is `lift (𝟙 N) 1 : N ⟶ N ⊗ G`, which is a group homomorphism. This is exactly the standard inclusion of the normal factor.

The setting (group objects in a cartesian monoidal category) is the natural one for internal semidirect products. The source and target types are correct: `Grp.mk N ⟶ A.semidirectProduct`.

Mathlib has no internal semidirect product of group objects. The only grep hit for "semidirect" under `Mathlib/CategoryTheory` is in `Action.lean`, which is about action groupoids and unrelated. Mathlib's `SemidirectProduct.inl` is the ordinary group version that this definition lifts.
